result:
Leaf certificates now get their AuthorityKeyIdentifier from the issuing CA's SubjectKeyIdentifier. I haven't run the tests, as you asked.

The leaf-cert code already added an AuthorityKeyIdentifier, but it derived the value by hashing the CA's public key. That matches the CA's SubjectKeyIdentifier only when the CA generated its own identifier the same way. A user-supplied CA with a different identifier would get a mismatched value.

In `dummy_cert` in `mitmproxy/certs.py`, it now reads the CA's SubjectKeyIdentifier extension and builds the AuthorityKeyIdentifier from it. If the CA has no SubjectKeyIdentifier, it falls back to the old public-key derivation.

I left the leaf without its own SubjectKeyIdentifier, as before. The existing comment says a leaf SKI matching the CA's breaks SChannel (issue 6494).

In `test/mitmproxy/test_certs.py`, `TestDummyCert.test_with_ca` now asserts that the leaf's AuthorityKeyIdentifier `key_identifier` equals the CA's SubjectKeyIdentifier digest.

diff --git a/mitmproxy/certs.py b/mitmproxy/certs.py
index 2f421e25e..321657d8b 100644
--- a/mitmproxy/certs.py
+++ b/mitmproxy/certs.py
@@ -356,10 +356,16 @@ def dummy_cert(
     )
 
     # https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5280#section-4.2.1.1
-    builder = builder.add_extension(
-        x509.AuthorityKeyIdentifier.from_issuer_public_key(cacert.public_key()),  # type: ignore
-        critical=False,
-    )
+    # Copy the keyIdentifier from the issuing CA's SKI if it has one (RFC 5280 §4.2.1.2),
+    # otherwise derive it from the CA's public key.
+    try:
+        ca_ski = cacert.extensions.get_extension_for_class(
+            x509.SubjectKeyIdentifier
+        ).value
+        aki = x509.AuthorityKeyIdentifier.from_issuer_subject_key_identifier(ca_ski)
+    except x509.ExtensionNotFound:
+        aki = x509.AuthorityKeyIdentifier.from_issuer_public_key(cacert.public_key())  # type: ignore
+    builder = builder.add_extension(aki, critical=False)
     # If CA and leaf cert have the same Subject Key Identifier, SChannel breaks in funny ways,
     # see https://github.com/mitmproxy/mitmproxy/issues/6494.
     # https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5280#section-4.2.1.2 states
